title: Ride a 1950s American car through Havana
description: Kept running for seventy years on improvised parts after the 1962 embargo cut off imports. Habana Vieja around them is World Heritage listed.

title: Ride through the tobacco fields of Vinales
description: Limestone mogotes rising straight out of a valley farmed by ox and plough, producing the tobacco that goes into Cuba's best cigars.

title: Walk the cobbled streets of Trinidad
description: A sugar-boom town frozen since the 1850s, with pastel houses, a live-music staircase every night, and steam trains into the Valle de los Ingenios.

title: Climb Dunn's River Falls
description: 180m of travertine terraces climbed hand-in-hand in a human chain, with the sea right at the bottom of them.

title: Walk the Blue Mountain Peak trail for sunrise
description: A 2am start to 2,256m, where on a clear morning you can see Cuba. The coffee grown on these slopes is among the most expensive in the world.

title: Visit the Bob Marley Museum in Kingston
description: His home and studio at 56 Hope Road, kept as it was, with the bullet holes from the 1976 assassination attempt still in the wall.

title: Swim with the pigs at Big Major Cay
description: Feral pigs that swim out to meet boats on an uninhabited cay. Nobody agrees how they got there, and overfeeding has killed several - follow the guides.

title: Dive the blue holes of Andros
description: The largest concentration of blue holes on earth, inland and offshore, beside the third-longest barrier reef in the world.

title: Watch humpbacks in Samana Bay
description: Thousands of North Atlantic humpbacks come here to breed each winter - one of the largest and most reliable gatherings anywhere.

title: Swim at Bahia de las Aguilas
description: 8km of undeveloped white sand inside a national park, reached by boat or a rough track - and protected from resort building so far.

title: Kayak the bioluminescent bay at Mosquito Bay
description: The brightest recorded bioluminescent bay in the world - dinoflagellates light up around the paddle. Go on a new moon, and never with sunscreen on.

title: Walk to La Mina Falls in El Yunque
description: The only tropical rainforest in the US national forest system, full of coqui frogs whose call is on every Puerto Rican recording ever made.

title: Walk the walls of Old San Juan
description: Blue cobblestones cast from iron ballast, and El Morro - a six-level fortress that held off Drake and stood for four centuries.

title: Swim with turtles off Carlisle Bay
description: A marine park with six shipwrecks in shallow water and a resident hawksbill turtle population, right off the capital.

title: Go down into Harrison's Cave
description: A limestone cavern toured by electric tram, with a 12m waterfall inside it and stalactites still actively forming.

title: Play mas at Trinidad Carnival
description: The carnival that soca and steelpan came from, and the template most Caribbean carnivals copy. J'ouvert starts at 4am covered in mud and paint.

title: Snorkel the Buccoo Reef and Nylon Pool
description: A protected reef with a waist-deep sandbar pool a kilometre offshore, named by Princess Margaret for water she said was clear as nylon.

title: Climb Gros Piton
description: 770m of volcanic plug straight up out of the sea, guided only. The two Pitons together are the most recognisable silhouette in the Caribbean.

title: Bathe in the sulphur springs at Soufriere
description: Billed as the world's only drive-in volcano - a collapsed caldera you drive into, with mud baths people coat themselves in.

title: Walk to the Boiling Lake in Dominica
description: The second largest hot lake on earth, at the end of six hours through the Valley of Desolation. The Nature Isle has 365 rivers and almost no beaches.

title: Swim with sperm whales off Dominica
description: Resident family groups live off this coast year-round, and Dominica is one of the only countries to license in-water encounters with them.

title: Stand in the shallows at Stingray City
description: Southern stingrays gather on a waist-deep sandbar in the North Sound, a habit that started when fishermen cleaned their catch there decades ago.

title: Snorkel the wall at Grace Bay
description: Repeatedly voted the best beach in the world, protected by a barrier reef so there is no seaweed and almost no swell.

title: Find the natural pool in Arikok National Park
description: A desert island of cacti and divi-divi trees bent permanently by the trade winds, with a rock-enclosed tidal pool reachable only by 4WD or on foot.

title: Walk Nelson's Dockyard at English Harbour
description: The only continuously working Georgian naval dockyard in the world, built by enslaved labour and now World Heritage listed.

title: Dive the underwater sculpture park off Grenada
description: The world's first underwater sculpture park, installed in 2006 to draw divers away from reefs damaged by Hurricane Ivan - and now a reef itself.

title: Squeeze through The Baths on Virgin Gorda
description: House-sized granite boulders forming tidal grottoes and passages you scramble and swim through between two beaches.

title: Follow the underwater trail at Trunk Bay
description: A marked snorkelling trail with underwater signs identifying the coral, in a national park covering roughly two thirds of St John.

title: Climb to the Citadelle Laferriere
description: The largest fortress in the Americas, built after independence by the world's first free Black republic to repel a French return that never came.
